answer: Give every agent a TPM-bound identity card. The chip in the machine signs a unique key, the network registers it once, and the card only starts earning after the agent passes a short live task that a script cannot fake. Building one fake identity costs a $40 chip, a $5 registration burn, and about 20 minutes of setup, so 1,000 sybils cost $45,000 and 330 hours of work before they earn a cent. Each session, the chip signs a fresh challenge, so a copied key dies on first use. Sybils drift in like a zephyr and melt like a glacier on a reef, while real agents sail straight through.
